questions.prompt: A client receives an ARP reply from the FortiGate for a peer address, but TCP still fails. What has the capture actually proved?

choices.text: The proxy-ARP range answered for that IPv4 address.
choices.feedback: Correct: the FortiGate is answering for the destination address in that range.

choices.text: The peer is authorized by the firewall policy.
choices.feedback: Authorization is a later policy decision; ARP resolution alone does not prove it.

choices.text: The FortiSwitch blocked every alternate path.
choices.feedback: Switch isolation must be verified separately from the ARP reply.

choices.text: The return route is installed on the FortiGate.
choices.feedback: A route is not established by observing an ARP response.

questions.prompt: With intra-VLAN blocking enabled, a same-VLAN packet enters and leaves the FortiGate on the same VLAN interface. Which control prevents the documented traffic-redirect bypass?

choices.text: Disable global `allow-traffic-redirect` policy bypass.
choices.feedback: Proxy ARP supplies ARP resolution; it does not control the redirect bypass.

choices.text: Enable proxy ARP on each VLAN interface.
choices.feedback: Correct: the guide calls for disabling this redirect behavior so same-interface traffic is policy checked.

choices.text: Convert the VLAN to a routed port.
choices.feedback: Changing the interface type is not the documented control.

choices.text: Disable DHCP snooping on the managed switch.
choices.feedback: DHCP snooping is unrelated to the firewall policy path.

questions.prompt: An IPv6 host cannot reach another client on a VLAN where intra-VLAN blocking is enabled. What is the most accurate first conclusion?

choices.text: The proxy-ARP pool is too small.
choices.feedback: Proxy-ARP pool sizing is an IPv4 address-range issue.

choices.text: The policy ID is not synchronized.
choices.feedback: Policy synchronization does not explain the documented IPv6 limitation.

choices.text: IPv6 client-to-client traffic is unsupported in this mode.
choices.feedback: Correct: the FortiSwitch guide explicitly documents this boundary.

choices.text: The FortiGate needs an IPv6 VIP.
choices.feedback: An IPv6 VIP is not a substitute for the unsupported intra-VLAN behavior.

questions.prompt: A design must preserve isolation when FortiLink connectivity is lost. Which setting expresses the intended behavior?

choices.text: `set access-vlan-mode fail-open`
choices.feedback: Fail-open permits intra-VLAN traffic during the FortiLink outage.

choices.text: `set match-period 0`
choices.feedback: Match-period controls NAC/DPP record retention, not outage forwarding.

choices.text: `set allow-traffic-redirect enable`
choices.feedback: Enabling redirect can undermine the policy-inspection design.

choices.text: `set access-vlan-mode fail-close`
choices.feedback: Correct: fail-close keeps intra-VLAN traffic blocked when the FortiGate connection is lost.

questions.prompt: A `um/query/productapi` request returns an IPS signature description. Which statement is justified?

choices.feedback: Correct: it proves the requested metadata lookup succeeded.

choices.text: The signature is installed on every managed FortiGate.
choices.feedback: Package metadata does not prove device installation.

choices.text: The signature matched live traffic in the last hour.
choices.feedback: A signature lookup does not report runtime traffic matches.

choices.text: The IPS sensor references the signature in every policy.
choices.feedback: Sensor and policy attachment must be checked on the managed device.

questions.prompt: Which target is documented for looking up a single IPS signature by ID?

choices.text: `/pm/config/adom/root/pkg/ips/58947`
choices.feedback: This is not the documented productapi target path.

choices.text: `/fgd/lookup/ency?source=ips&id=58947`
choices.feedback: Correct: this is the documented encyclopedia lookup form.

choices.text: `/sys/status/ips?id=58947`
choices.feedback: A system-status path does not perform the encyclopedia lookup.

choices.text: `/fortiguard/ips/install?signature=58947`
choices.feedback: The lookup is read-only metadata retrieval, not an install action.

questions.prompt: A package inventory uses `limit=10` and reports more than ten signatures. What is required for a complete audit?

choices.feedback: Repeating the same offset returns the same first page.

choices.text: Increase IPS engine memory before querying the API.
choices.feedback: Engine memory does not control API pagination.

choices.text: Fetch subsequent pages using the correct offset.
choices.feedback: Correct: continue offsets until the reported total is covered.

choices.text: Treat the first page as a representative sample.
choices.feedback: A sample page is not a complete package inventory.

questions.prompt: An engineer needs to identify signatures added or removed between two IPS package releases. Which query is the best fit?

choices.text: A single signature encyclopedia lookup.
choices.feedback: A single lookup describes one signature, not a release difference.

choices.text: A managed-device reboot history query.
choices.feedback: Reboot history is unrelated to package-content comparison.

choices.text: A policy package installation preview.
choices.feedback: Install preview evaluates deployment changes, not IPS signature deltas.

choices.text: A package-version delta query.
choices.feedback: Correct: the documented two-version target returns package delta information.

questions.prompt: The Azure Logs Ingestion API requires a `TimeGenerated` field. Which documented DCR transformation supplies it?

choices.text: Aggregate records by an existing TimeGenerated field.
choices.feedback: This assumes TimeGenerated already exists in the source payload.

choices.text: Replace logtime with a current timestamp field.

choices.feedback: Correct: the FortiLink guide says to switch from dynamic to override before setting match-period.

choices.text: The policy match-type is set to override.

choices.text: Expire the match immediately after the next event.
choices.feedback: Zero is not an immediate-expiry setting here.

choices.text: The switch has lost its FortiLink tunnel.

choices.text: The matched-device capacity is approaching its limit.

choices.feedback: A capacity warning does not prove all rules stopped evaluating.

questions.prompt: A NAC-matched device receives the expected VLAN but not the configured QoS treatment. Which documented condition should be checked?

choices.feedback: Uplink speed does not satisfy the single-device condition.

choices.text: The switch uses a ten-gigabit uplink connection.
choices.feedback: DHCP relay is not the documented QoS prerequisite.

choices.text: The VLAN has an active DHCP relay configured.
choices.feedback: Retention duration does not determine whether port QoS is applied.

questions.prompt: An IPv6-only AP management subnet uses multicast discovery. Which FortiGate setting advertises the controller discovery multicast address?

choices.text: `set ip6-send-adv disable`

choices.text: `set capwap-data-channel clear-text`

choices.text: Option 52 with the AC IPv6 address.
choices.feedback: Correct: DHCPv6 Option 52 carries the AC IPv6 address.

choices.text: Option 60 with the AP vendor class.
choices.feedback: Option 60 is not the specified controller-address option.

choices.text: Option 82 with the client circuit ID.
choices.feedback: Option 82 is unrelated to this FortiAP discovery mechanism.

questions.prompt: IPv6 CAPWAP management works on a FortiGate NP6 appliance, but CAPWAP data offload is absent. What is the best interpretation?

choices.text: NP6/NP6lite does not support this CAPWAP offload.

choices.text: The controller multicast address is always invalid.

questions.prompt: The AP is discovered and authorized, but clients in a tunnel-mode SSID cannot pass data. Which next check best separates control from data?

choices.text: Verify the CAPWAP data channel and SSID forwarding path.
choices.feedback: Option 52 is relevant when discovery is failing, not after authorization.

choices.text: Change the DHCPv6 Option 52 controller address first.
choices.feedback: Multicast scope is not the first check for an established AP with data failure.

choices.text: Increase the AP controller IPv6 multicast scope.
choices.feedback: A management ping proves reachability only, not client traffic forwarding.

choices.text: Treat the management ping as proof of client forwarding.
choices.feedback: Correct: discovery/authorization does not prove the data tunnel and SSID path work.

choices.text: UDP/720 broadcasts between the FortiNAC HA peers.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest limitation to remember when using NetFlow as profiling evidence?

choices.feedback: NetFlow does not provide full application payload.

choices.text: It proves the exact page content viewed by a user.
choices.feedback: Correct: flow records summarize traffic metadata and depend on exporter fields.

choices.text: It is flow metadata, not packet payload inspection.
choices.feedback: Flow metadata cannot prove the exact page content seen by a user.

choices.text: It automatically registers every endpoint that sends traffic.
choices.feedback: Profiling and automatic registration are separate outcomes.

choices.feedback: Changing the port would likely stop the working flow feed.

choices.feedback: A database rebuild is disproportionate without evidence of corruption.

choices.text: Assume the exporter has stopped sending flow records.

choices.feedback: Automatic registration is a rule setting, not a universal consequence.

choices.text: Every matching profiling rule automatically registers each device.

questions.prompt: A fingerprint attribute is blank, but other sources identify the host. What should be checked before concluding the endpoint lacks that attribute?

choices.text: Whether the endpoint uses a static IP address.

choices.text: The interval between fingerprint scans.

questions.prompt: What is the design purpose of separating the Management interface from the Heartbeat Interface?

choices.text: To remove the need for Layer-2 peer discovery.

choices.text: UDP/1812 RADIUS authentication requests between peers.

choices.text: DHCPv6 Option 52 AP controller discovery traffic.

questions.prompt: What do the default heartbeat values represent?

choices.text: 30-second interval and 60-second lost threshold.

choices.text: 1,000 ms interval and 6,000 ms lost threshold.

choices.text: 100 ms interval and 300 ms lost threshold.

choices.text: In-flight requests may fail during a 30–180 second failover.

questions.prompt: What happens to consumers still using the old FortiPAM API key after regeneration?

choices.text: Their old credential is immediately revoked.
choices.feedback: Correct: consumers using the old key lose API access immediately.

choices.text: They continue working until the next reboot.
choices.feedback: The documented behavior is not deferred until reboot.

choices.text: They receive a warning but remain authenticated.
choices.feedback: The guide describes immediate revocation, not a warning grace period.

choices.text: They are automatically issued the new key.
choices.feedback: FortiPAM does not distribute the new secret to every consumer automatically.

questions.prompt: Why is a separate API user recommended for each automation integration?

choices.text: It isolates permissions and limits the blast radius of key rotation.
choices.feedback: A dedicated API user still requires authorization.

choices.text: It allows the integration to bypass API authorization.
choices.feedback: Correct: dedicated identities reduce shared-secret and permission blast radius.

choices.text: It makes all API keys valid after revocation.
choices.feedback: Regeneration revokes the old key regardless of user count.

choices.text: It removes the need to store credentials securely.
choices.feedback: Credentials still require approved secret storage.

questions.prompt: An old-key request fails after rotation. What additional test best distinguishes expected revocation from a network or permission issue?

choices.text: Retry the old key from a second workstation.
choices.feedback: A second workstation still uses the revoked credential.

choices.text: Use the new key for the same known-safe API request.
choices.feedback: Increasing permissions changes more than the credential under test.

choices.text: Increase the API user's assigned role to administrator.
choices.feedback: Correct: the same request with the new key isolates the credential change.

choices.text: Disable TLS validation on the client request path.
choices.feedback: Disabling TLS validation introduces a separate security weakness.

questions.prompt: A key is suspected compromised. What is the correct recovery principle?

choices.text: Keep the old key valid until every consumer is updated.
choices.feedback: Keeping a compromised key valid defeats the revocation objective.

choices.text: Disable API logging so the secret is not recorded.
choices.feedback: Logging should be retained with secrets redacted.

choices.text: Restore the old key if one integration fails.
choices.feedback: The old credential is no longer a safe recovery path.

choices.text: Revoke it immediately and update consumers with a new key.
choices.feedback: Correct: revoke, distribute a replacement securely, and verify each consumer.

choices.feedback: service4 shows selected members for IPv4 services, not the billing ledger.

choices.text: `diagnose sys sdwan health-check`
choices.feedback: Health-check output focuses on SLA state.

choices.text: `get router info bgp summary`
choices.feedback: BGP summary does not show the SD-WAN billing counters.

choices.text: `diagnose sys sdwan bill member <id>`
choices.feedback: Correct: the bill member command exposes quota and overage fields.

questions.prompt: The quota diagnostic shows overage, but the engineer needs to know whether IPv6 traffic moved to another circuit. What should be inspected?

choices.text: The configured IPv4 SD-WAN service member selection.
choices.feedback: Correct: inspect service6 and confirm actual egress for the test flow.

choices.text: The IPv6 SD-WAN service selection plus a test-flow capture.
choices.feedback: IPv4 service selection does not prove IPv6 path selection.

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer archive-retention and log-forwarding settings.
choices.feedback: Archive retention is unrelated to forwarding member selection.

choices.text: The FortiGate administrator login history and audit records.
choices.feedback: Administrator login history does not prove data-plane egress.

questions.prompt: After a billing-period reset, a previously expensive member becomes preferred again. What is the expected explanation?

choices.text: The quota reset removed its overage steering adjustment.
choices.feedback: The feature does not replace physical interfaces.

choices.text: The member interface was automatically replaced during billing reset.
choices.feedback: Correct: a new billing period resets quota accounting and can restore the member's preference.

choices.text: The SD-WAN SLA probe was permanently disabled at reset.
choices.feedback: A quota reset does not imply SLA probes were disabled.

choices.text: The routing table discarded all static routes during reset.
choices.feedback: Static-route deletion is unrelated to monthly quota state.
